title: observability-snapshot-exporter-and-alert-mixdown
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Long-tail incidents often require a compact, queryable snapshot of an invocation (tokens, top-level spans, prompt shape, cost estimate) to triage without pulling full traces. This PR adds a lightweight observability snapshot exporter that periodically writes compact invocation snapshots to the telemetry store, and introduces an alert-mixdown mechanism that reduces noisy alerting by weighting route-level signals and optionally attaching sampled snapshots to alerts.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a snapshotter service that emits compact invocation documents (invocation_id, timestamp, route, prompt_shape_hash, token_counts, estimated_token_cost, top_n_error_spans, pre/post-kv-warm flags). Adds a minimal sidecar exporter to the telemetry pipeline for fast writes. Adds alert-mixdown rules that: (1) apply per-route weight and quiet window; (2) attach one sampled snapshot per alert group when severity >= warning; (3) allow per-tenant opt-out. Adds a Grafana dashboard and a focused playbook for oncall. Updates docs with configuration knobs and upgrade notes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement snapshotter runtime and config schema
- [x] Export compact snapshot docs to telemetry index with bounded retention
- [x] Hook snapshot attachment into alerting pipeline with rate limits
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for sample selection
- [x] Add dashboard + runbook pages
- [x] Add Linear links for rollout and opt-out controls

Backward compatibility & safety: Snapshots are opt-in per-tenant by default off; when enabled snapshots are written to the existing telemetry index under a new type (invocation_snapshot_v1) with TTL. The alert-mixdown is configurable and disabled by default for existing alerts. No breaking public API changes.

Related: ENG-5732 (observability long-tail), ENG-5778 (alerting noise reduction).

release_notes: Adds a new optional invocation snapshot exporter (invocation_snapshot_v1) that teams can enable per-tenant to speed long-tail debugging; introduces alert-mixdown to reduce noisy alerts by route weighting and optional snapshot attachment. Config knobs: max_snapshot_bytes, snapshot_ttl_days, alert_mixdown_weights. Disabled by default; see docs/observability/snapshots.md for upgrade steps.
notes_for_ops: Staging rollout plan: enable on a low-traffic tenant and observe telemetry index growth; verify opt-out works; validate alert-mixdown reduces duplicate alerts. Monitor telemetry_write_errors and snapshot_retention_gauge. Nightly job to drop old snapshots runs via existing TTL; we also added a manual housekeeper endpoint in sidecar for emergency trimming.
security_considerations: Snapshots scrub user PII by default: the serializer strips high-entropy fields in prompt metadata and truncates any free-text to 512 bytes. Tenants with stricter retention should use per-tenant opt-out and KMS-backed telemetry stores if required. Security review done by Arjun (notes in ENG-5778).
notes_for_release_engineering: No infra schema migration required; mapping added is non-destructive and uses a new index/type. Recommend a canary rollout for 48 hours with per-tenant opt-in. Update observability Helm chart to include sidecar image tag. See charts/observability/README for values.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover snapshot size trimming, sample selector determinism, and opt-out config. Integration tests exercise exporter + telemetry index mapping in a local test cluster. Stress test added to run 10k synthetic invocations and validate sample rate and retention enforcement.
upgrade_impact: Low. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default. Turning it on will write additional docs to telemetry; operators should verify retention TTL and expected storage. No API contract changes.
notes_for_support: If customers see unexpected snapshot growth, check snapshot_ttl_days and opt-out flags; run sidecar housekeeper endpoint to trim. If alerts stop attaching snapshots, verify tenant opt-in and alert-mixdown weights are configured.
